findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body: `recordIssuedToken` passes the complete issued token to `audit`, which writes it to `console.log`. In deployments that collect console output, anyone with log access could recover and replay live bearer tokens.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` is influenced by a request or query parameter, an absolute attacker-controlled URL now redirects authenticated users off-site. Accept only same-origin paths or explicitly trusted origins to prevent open-redirect phishing.

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to audit logs
findings.body:
Every call records the complete token via `console.log`. When real bearer/session tokens are issued and production console output is collected or accessible, log readers can replay those credentials and impersonate users.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body:
Passing an absolute attacker-controlled URL such as `https://evil.example` now redirects the authenticated user off-site. If `returnUrl` originates from a request/query parameter, this creates an open redirect suitable for login-flow phishing; allow only same-origin paths or explicitly trusted origins.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Validate login return URLs before navigation
findings.body:
Any attacker-controlled `returnUrl` (for example, `https://evil.example`) now redirects users off-site after login, enabling phishing and credential/token theft; dangerous schemes such as `javascript:` may also execute in the page context where browser policy permits.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every call passes the raw issued token to `console.log`. In environments where console output is collected or accessible to operators and support tooling, anyone with broader log access can recover live bearer tokens and impersonate users.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
